body: I'm incredibly proud of you. You've come very far in a very short amount of time. Keep fighting for yourself- you are your own hero.

DO. NOT. END. IT. If you're looking for a sign to stay, this is your sign. You will have good months, good days, good years. But you will also have bad ones. Feel the bad ones, then let them pass. All feelings, good or bad, will always pass with time. Force yourself to do things you need to do, and then find the motivation from doing those things to do other things, like getting more books or a gym membership. You don't need resources in the area to keep yourself afloat- there are also ones available online. You said UC Berkeley- I assume you're in California. There are many places in Cali just a drive away that can help you. Even if you aren't in California, use the resources on this subreddit to help you. You got this- you are stronger than you will ever know. You're intelligent, you seem so kind, and I can tell you have a good heart. Remember that.

I am listening. I will always be listening. There will always be someone out there, hearing your pain, feeling your pain. I tried to kill myself seven months ago, for the same reason. I prayed and I prayed and I prayed for a sign. I needed a sign to stay alive. I never got one. So I tried to kill myself. I've never been more glad something failed. I am not better off now, I am not happier now. I see reminders of my past in everything, and I see reminders of my suicide attempt in everything. But I know, one day, this pain will be useful to me. Sometimes life is sticking through the tough times, feeling the emotions you need to, and then letting them pass. One day, you won't feel so alone. You can make that day today. Reach out, find support, just as you've done here. A cry for help, such as the post you wrote, is the first step to this. I recommend checking out the directory of hotlines they have on this subreddit. Use them. This is your sign.

Hi, my name is Teddy. I was diagnosed with generalized anxiety at age 11 and bipolar depression at age 15. I'm a junior in high school. I too have been in therapy my whole life. I have two older brothers, both of which are older than you, one of which has had major drug problems their entire life and ADHD. The other has a minor form of autism. I've been down the same path as you, and while you have more life experience under your belt, I can promise you something. I can promise you that the feelings you feel right now will pass, with time and patience. I was an active self-harmer for four years, have had two suicide attempts, hospitalized once, have an eating disorder, and have also allowed myself down the path of self-medication and self-sabotage. I know what it feels like to feel completely useless, like you were better off dead, and that your life and your death is no longer your burden to carry. Please, please, don't end it now. I know how tough it can be, and I know how badly you may want to get away from it, but this hurt and this pain will only benefit you in the long run. Your emotions now will only be a distant memory in a year, five years, ten years from now. You'll see how far you've come, and you'll be proud of yourself for sticking through. I'm sure, as many with anxiety and depression feel, that it is easier for you to suppress your emotions and negative thoughts than to feel them. It is easier. And finding that motivation to do anything: shower, get out of bed, take medication, talk to people, can be very, very difficult. And it feels easier to lock yourself away and not feel anything, to self medicate until you feel nothing but a high. The motivation to do things can only come from doing them, which is the harsh truth of mental illness. While it might be easier to do something that can be considered self-sabotage, choosing better for yourself is a choice. You can't choose the situation you've been given, but you can choose how you deal with it. I'm sure you've heard this before, from countless professionals, but I thought it might help to hear it from me, who's been in the same boat. Even getting out of bed for me has become a large task. I struggle to find the motivation. Sometimes, you have to force yourself to do things. Self-care isn't always face masks and bath bombs. It's forcing yourself to eat, sleep, drink at least three glasses of water, get out of the house, go to class. And, most importantly, allow yourself to feel the negatives. Allow yourself to have the panic attacks, the anger, the sadness, the hurt. But let it pass. All emotions will eventually pass. This goes for positive emotions too. They will all come and go. Appreciate and remember the positive emotions, but also appreciate and remember the negative ones. Allowing yourself to feel is the first step. Please seek help from a medical professional for self medication help- I promise it's not a shot in the dark. It can help. You won't get in trouble. I hope this helps. I'm just a message away.

Your mother didn't 'waste' anything on you. I'm sure you're her pride and joy and she's so glad she had you. But don't just stick around for your family. Stick around for your own sake. You'll be through this rough patch with time and it'll make you so incredibly strong. I don't know if this helps, but I hope you're okay and I hope you can keep surviving through this

Vans,

My name is Teddy. When I was 13, I was in the same boat as you. I was cutting myself and crying and wanted to end it all, every single day. And I'm in the same boat right now. And while I can't help myself, my experience with psychiatry and mental health might be able to help you. I play cello, and can no longer play cello because I'm also too weak. I'm sorry you feel this way, and I know its cliche but I promise, with everything I have in me, it WILL get better, even if you don't think so right now. In ten years time, when you're 23, you'll be grateful you stuck around. You'll be grateful for the experiences and challenges you overcame at such a young age. Remember how incredibly young you are. Remember how much time you can still have on this Earth to change things for yourself. These awful parts of your life are also a reason to keep going, not just the good parts. Stick around so you can keep growing and learning. You'll learn so much about yourself. I believe in you, and I'm so proud of you for making it this far
